review_scope: Republic of Cyprus civil-procedure subset: published 2023 Rules, Part 34. Transitional rules, later amendments and criminal proceedings require separate verification.

appointment.summary_en: Expert evidence is controlled by the court; Rules 34.8–34.9 provide for a single joint expert and instructions.

items_en: Qualifications; literature or other material relied on.
Material facts and instructions, distinguishing personal knowledge.
Who performed examinations or tests, their qualifications and supervision.
Range of relevant opinions, reasons for the expert's view, conclusions and reservations.
Confirmation of compliance with the duty to the court and a statement of truth.

rights_duties.summary_en: Provide objective assistance within the expert's field; disclose material changes of opinion.

statute.title_en: Civil Procedure Rules 2023, Part 34; official Gazette publication of 3 July 2023

timestamp.qualified_recognition: Qualified timestamps carry date/time accuracy and data-integrity presumptions; qualification requires the statutory conditions.

open_questions: Provider qualification, certificate status, national filing rules and supported signature formats must be checked separately; this profile does not qualify a TgWitness signature or timestamp.
Verify commencement, transitional application and amendments for the relevant case; the 2021 technical-assistance draft was not used as enacted law.
The exact current statement-of-truth form and signing instructions require local review; this profile records the requirement but supplies no invented declaration.
Criminal expert evidence is not covered. The Republic of Cyprus profile must not be treated as a separate legal profile for proceedings outside its effective administration.
Report requirements are summarised in English. Native expert/law terms do not imply a complete reviewed translation of the report or interface.
court_language_notes: Constitution Article 3 governs Greek/Turkish judicial use. The 2022 constitutional amendment permits English in specified Commercial Court and Admiralty Court proceedings under statutory conditions; English is not a general filing option.
